attempts.raw: TEXT The dot product of two vectors geometrically represents the product of the magnitude of one vector and the projection of the other vector onto it. Specifically, if vectors **a** and **b** have an angle θ between them, then their dot product **a · b = |a||b|cos(θ)**. This means the dot product measures how much one vector extends in the direction of the other. When the vectors are orthogonal (perpendicular), θ = 90°, so cos(90°) = 0, and their dot product is zero, indicating no projection of one vector onto the other. If the dot product is negative, it means the angle between the vectors is greater than 90° but less than 180°, so the projection of one vector onto the other points in the opposite direction, reflecting a negative component along that axis.
